bytes.title: Toll-takers earn 5 to 9 times the market's margin

bytes.kicker: Battery storage · demand vs Indian cell supply
bytes.title: India's storage boom still runs on imported cells
bytes.dek: Storage could reach about 302 GWh by FY32 from 6.3 GWh in FY26 (industry estimate). ACME's ~19 GWh of batteries on order are all Chinese, Amara Raja still imports ~70% of its cells and Indian cells cost 5–15% more.
bytes.read: Until a local-content rule or incentive closes the 5–15% gap, the first wave of Indian storage will be built on Chinese cells.
bytes.sources: Vantage analysis of Q1–Q2 FY27 earnings calls of ACME Solar, Exide Industries, Amara Raja and Waaree Energies; industry estimates; Vantage sector intel, 21 Nov 2026
bytes.notes: The FY32 storage figure (302 GWh, from 6.3 GWh in FY26) and the ~90% import share are industry estimates, not company data. Demand columns are from ACME's Q2 FY27 call: about 19 GWh of batteries contracted with CATL, Hithium, Ganfeng, Trina and CLOU; FY27 commissioning target raised to over 12 GWh; and SECI's 4 GW / 16 GWh peak-power auction. Cell columns: Exide's 6 GWh lithium-ion plant was commissioned on 23 September 2026, but its large-format storage-cell line waits on incentive clarity; Amara Raja's 5 GWh LFP cell plant was approved this quarter with about 30 months to build; Waaree's 3.5 GWh cell pilot is due from Q4 FY27 and its 16.5 GWh second phase is in planning, with funding tied to policy. Cost gaps are on a landed basis as stated by management; ACME's call describes the January change as a 6% Chinese export tax, Exide's as the end of a 6% export rebate.

bytes.kicker: Shipbuilding · naval programmes still in tender

bytes.kicker: Market valuation · Sensex earnings vs price, Oct 2021–Oct 2026
bytes.title: Sensex earnings rose 11% in a year. The index fell 11%.
bytes.dek: Trailing Sensex EPS rose 10.7% to ₹3,742 in the year to October 2026, while the index fell 11.3% to 74,460. The trailing P/E dropped from 24.8x to 19.9x as foreign investors sold a net ₹2.95 lakh cr of equities.
bytes.read: This year's fall came from a lower multiple, not lower profits: the index now costs a fifth less per rupee of earnings than a year ago.
bytes.sources: BSE Sensex closing levels; Sensex trailing consolidated EPS; NSDL/CDSL FPI flow data; consensus forward estimates; Vantage analysis
bytes.notes: Index levels are Sensex closes at end-October each year (30 Oct 2026 was the month's last trading day). Trailing EPS is 12-month consolidated earnings per index unit; it equals the index level divided by the trailing P/E (74,460 ÷ 19.9x), so the five-year EPS growth is 82% (12.7% a year) against 26% for the index (4.7% a year). P/E series built on other EPS bases, such as those published by data vendors, read higher (about 21x in November 2026) but show the same fall. The forward P/E uses consensus 12-month-forward earnings estimates, which are forecasts and get revised. Foreign flows are net equity flows from depository data for January–October 2026 (₹34,843 cr in October); early-November tallies ranged from ₹2.95 to about ₹3.1 lakh cr depending on the cut-off and whether primary-market buying is netted.

bytes.kicker: Management changes · the first call after a CEO, CFO or MD change
bytes.title: New boss, new tone: the first call after a change
bytes.dek: NIIT's call score fell from 63 to 41 on its first call under a new CEO, who cut the FY27 revenue view to flat; Apollo Tyres and SKF India (Industrial) dropped to the 40 cap, while South Indian Bank rose from 58 to 61.
bytes.read: The first call under new leadership is often where guidance gets reset; NIIT's 60–90 day review makes its Q3 call the next marker.
bytes.sources: Vantage analysis of management-change filings on BSE and Q4 FY26–Q2 FY27 earnings calls; Q2 FY27 results filed on BSE
bytes.notes: Vantage call score (0–100) on the last call before a CEO, CFO or MD change was filed vs the first call after it. A score of 40 is the cap applied when a call drops guidance without explanation or carries a serious red flag: Apollo Tyres dropped its full-year Europe EBITDA guide on its Q2 call. NIIT named Anish Sarkar CEO on 14 Oct 2026; on the 3 Nov call the company said: “we are, at this point of time, looking at the rest of the year and going by the experience of this quarter, assuming that the revenue is likely to be broadly flat.” Apollo Tyres' CFO resigned on 6 Oct and a new CFO was named on 4 Nov (call 6 Nov), in a quarter when raw-material costs rose about 25%. SKF India (Industrial) announced its MD handover on 11 Aug (effective 1 Sep), before its Q1 FY27 call; its score recovered to 55 on the Q2 call. South Indian Bank's new MD & CEO took over on 1 Oct; Info Edge announced its CEO exit on 28 Oct, two days before the call. Scores also reflect results, so a shift cannot be put down to the change alone.

bytes.kicker: Household savings · domestic flows vs foreign selling, Oct 2026
bytes.title: Households kept buying as foreign investors sold
bytes.dek: SIPs brought in ₹32,160 cr in October (+8.9% YoY) from 10 crore accounts, and equity funds had their 68th straight month of inflows, while foreign investors sold a net ₹2.95 lakh cr of Indian equities in Jan–Oct 2026.
